papers.title: Tenogenic Induction of Human MSCs by Anisotropically Aligned Collagen Biotextiles.
papers.abstract: A novel biofabrication modality, electrophoretic compaction with macromolecular alignment, was utilized to make collagen threads that mimic the native tendon's structure and mechanical properties. A device with kinematic electrodes was designed to fabricate collagen threads in continuous length. For the first time, a 3D-biotextile was woven purely from collagen. Mechanical properties and load-displacement behavior of the biotextile mimicked those of the native tendon while presenting a porosity of 80%. The open pore network facilitated cell seeding across the continuum of the bioscaffold. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) seeded in the woven scaffold underwent tenogenic differentiation in the absence of growth factors and synthesized a matrix that was positive for tenomodulin, COMP and type I collagen. Up-regulation of tenomodulin, a tendon specific marker, was 11.6 ± 3.5 fold, COMP was up-regulated 16.7 ± 5.5 fold, and Col I was up-regulated 6.9 ± 2.7 fold greater on ELAC threads when compared to randomly oriented collagen gels. These results demonstrate that a bioscaffold woven by using collagen threads with densely compacted and anisotropically aligned substrate texture stimulates tenogenesis topographically, rendering the electrochemically aligned collagen as a promising candidate for functional repair of tendons and ligaments.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究胶原蛋白生物纺织物的肌腱诱导，未涉及任何AI或生物打印流程。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML model, no bioprinting workflow integration, and no computational control or optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发仿生肌腱结构的胶原生物纺织物以诱导干细胞分化。
summary_zh.method: 使用电泳压实和分子排列制备连续胶原线，并编织成3D纺织物。
summary_zh.result: 纺织物力学性能类似天然肌腱，且无需生长因子即可诱导干细胞向肌腱分化。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学测试和干细胞分化标记物表达验证。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate a collagen biotextile that structurally and mechanically mimics native tendon for tenogenic induction without growth factors.
summary_en.method: Electrophoretic compaction with molecular alignment was used to produce continuous collagen threads, which were then woven into a 3D biotextile.
summary_en.result: The biotextile exhibited tendon-like mechanical properties and an 80% porosity, and seeded MSCs underwent tenogenic differentiation with upregulation of tenomodulin, COMP, and type I collagen.
summary_en.validation: Validation included mechanical testing and quantitative gene expression analysis of tendon-specific markers.
